reuse_traps: Triage finding constructor: `collision_finding` (crates/rs_cam_core/src/stock/sim_triage.rs, used at ~line 346) vs hand-built `Finding { dedup_key, diagnostic, occurrences, worst }` in `plunge_class_finding` (1552) and `rest_slower_than_fresh_finding` (~548). There is no single `Finding::new`; you would copy ~35 lines of struct literal. Only the safety/collision case has a helper.

Cached triage accessor: `SimulationState::cached_simulation_triage` (crates/rs_cam_viz/src/state/simulation/issue_triage.rs:59) versus calling `session.simulation_triage(...)` directly in the UI. A new panel row would re-build the triage per frame if you do not find the cache.

Percent-of-runtime figures: use the `AirCutRatios` trait (`s.air_cut_pct_of_total_runtime()`); sim_diagnostics.rs:~705 has a comment that a hand-written divide is a guarded sentry failure, but low-engagement is still a local divide. A new ratio metric will tempt you to write a closure.

Rapid/holder/obstacle location attribution: `AttributedRapidCollision` / `evidence.attributed_rapid_collisions()` (G-RAPIDFRAME) already maps global move to (toolpath, local move); `SimulationState::global_move_for_local` does the reverse for the jump click (sim_diagnostics.rs:~915). Easy to re-derive wrongly.

Spatial dedup helpers `dedup`, `cap_per_toolpath`, `bucket_edge_mm`, `spatial_bucket` in sim_triage.rs (used at ~lines 540-600) exist for advisories; a new advisory would be tempted to write its own capping.

Not-measured vs zero JSON handling: the `counts` nulling loop at crates/rs_cam_viz/src/controller/events/compute.rs:2569 and `cut_metrics_not_measured` (2447) are the only place that turns absent traces into null; a new numeric metric added outside `counts` must re-implement this.
Severity-to-role mapping: `warnings_badge` / `Role::Danger` vs `Role::Caution` in sim_diagnostics.rs (129, 870) is hard-coded by bucket, separate from `Severity` (diagnostics/mod.rs).
ambiguity: Two patterns for a sim warning: (a) direct triage finding built in sim_triage.rs (plunge_class_finding, rest_slower_than_fresh_finding, standing_material_finding, entry_load_finding, link_cut_finding); (b) VerdictKind + Verdict in session/compute/diagnostics.rs:1163-1471 mapped by the exhaustive adapter at from_project_diagnostics.rs:76 and flowing into triage.actions via the Class B loop. (b) is compiler-forced, (a) is not. Both reach the GUI and MCP.

Two things called 'issues' in the Warnings tab: triage findings (`SimulationTriage`, sim_diagnostics.rs:870) versus `SimulationIssueKind` cut-trace issues (sim_diagnostics.rs:660, state/simulation/issue_triage.rs:~215 and MCP `issues` array at app/mcp/simulation.rs:626-701). Both display in the same tab and the MCP has `issue_count` beside `triage`. The sim_triage.rs header says to use triage, but the issue-kind path looks equally plausible.

'Metric' vs 'warning': a metric lives in `ToolLoadReport`/`CriterionKind` cut-metric cards (sim_diagnostics.rs:1505 `has_cut_metric_card`, `CutMetricSpec` 1521, `DistributionMetric`) on the Metrics tab, a different pipeline from Warnings. A 'metric that appears in Warnings' could be copied from either; the summary pills (`CountPill`, sim_diagnostics.rs:~535-575) are a third place.

MCP exposure: `get_diagnostics`/`run_simulation` (build_mcp_diagnostics, compute.rs:2345) vs `get_project_diagnostics` (app/mcp/diagnostics.rs:~600-675 via diagnose_project_with_evidence, which does NOT include sim_triage-only findings) vs `get_toolpath_diagnostics` (diagnostics.rs:~690) vs `get_cut_trace` (app/mcp/simulation.rs). A triage-only finding appears in the first only; a verdict-route finding appears in several. Which one is 'the MCP simulation output' is not obvious.

Placement in Category/Severity/Confidence for the new Diagnostic: plunge_class_finding uses ToolLoad/Caution/Critical/Verified, rest_slower uses Efficiency/Info/Approximate, air-cut advisory uses Efficiency/Hint; there is no rule in code for choosing.
